title: Customer-anchorable quota resets with prorated rollover and cross-region failover handling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Some enterprise customers require quota resets to align to a customer-defined anchor (e.g., 04:00 local time, fiscal-month boundaries, or a contract-specific timestamp) rather than the platform default UTC month/day boundary. This interacts badly with reserved capacity windows, burst buckets, and multi-region failover: resets executed in different datacenters can desynchronize usage banking and cause transient overages or double-crediting. We need a robust, auditable mechanism that supports per-tenant anchors, prorated rollover (for mid-cycle subscription changes), preserves correctness during DST changes and leap-second edgecases, and provides deterministic behavior under cross-region failover.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable per-tenant quota anchor: admin API and Console setting that accepts timezone, anchor time-of-day, and optional monthly anchor day
Reset execution is deterministic and idempotent across regions: running the reset twice or in parallel never double-applies credits or clears the wrong counters
Reserved capacity interactions: reserved pools are adjusted atomically with tenant quotas during reset so usage accounting and billing reflect the correct available balance
Prorated rollover: when a customer changes quota mid-cycle (upgrade/downgrade), the remaining tokens are prorated and reflected in billing adjustments and invoiceable usage
Audit trail and reconciliation: every reset run creates an immutable ledger entry with before/after balances, region/instance that executed the reset, and a correlation id for follow-up investigation
Monitoring & alerts: SLO for reset success rate >= 99.9% and alerting for drift between regional views > 0.1% of tenant volume
Regression tests that simulate DST transitions, leap-second event, cross-region failover, and concurrent resets pass in CI
technical_design: Overview: Introduce a tenant-level 'anchor' configuration (timezone string, anchor_hour, anchor_minute, monthly_anchor_day optional). Convert anchor to a deterministic UTC reset instant for each tenant and cycle. Implementation components: 1) Anchor Resolver: deterministic function that maps tenant anchor + cycle identifier -> UTC reset timestamp; supports stable semantics across DST by resolving to wall-clock local time converted to UTC using IANA tz rules at the anchored date. 2) Reset Coordinator: a leader-elected process per-tenant using existing tenant-lease service (lease TTL) to ensure a single reset executor. 3) Two-phase reset operation: phase A (prepare) computes proration, locks relevant tenant ledger rows and reserved capacity allocations, writes a provisional ledger delta with correlation_id; phase B (commit) applies deltas atomically and releases locks. Writes are idempotent keyed by correlation_id. 4) Backoff and retry semantics: if leader steps down mid-reset, steps detect incomplete provisional entries and either complete or roll back via reconciliation job. 5) Reconciliation service: periodic job that compares expected anchor-derived balances across regions and emits corrective transactions if drift detected; corrections are tagged as automated-reconciliation with detailed audit notes. 6) Billing integration: the provisional ledger delta is synced to billing pipeline as a non-invoiceable adjustment flag; final commit flips flag to invoiceable where appropriate. 7) Reserved capacity handling: reserve pool counters are adjusted in the same transactional boundary as tenant quota changes using existing reserved-pools table and the same locking strategy to prevent double-allocation during near-simultaneous resets. 8) Observability: add timers and counters for reset duration, leader-election latency, reconciliation corrections, and per-tenant drift. 9) Safety: feature-flag gate to enable anchor-based resets per-customer; default tenant behavior is unchanged until migration window is complete.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: API and Console UI behind feature flag; enable for 5 pilot tenants with low volume. Phase 2: Run in read-only simulation mode for 2 weeks comparing simulated resets with current resets and collect drift metrics. Phase 3: Enable write-mode for pilots and run augmented reconciliation for 30 days. Phase 4: Gradually open to all tenants with opt-in migration workflow in Console that previews first three reset timestamps and estimated prorated credits. Failback: global feature-flag off will stop new anchor resets and reconciliation will attempt to roll forward provisional deltas to default-cycle alignment.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for Anchor Resolver covering DST boundary cases and end-of-month edgecases (28/29/30/31) and leap-second simulated conversions
Integration tests that bring up two regional replicas, force leader election flip during a reset, and assert ledger idempotence
Load tests: 50k tenant resets/day synthetic workload to validate performance of leader-election and reconciliation window
Billing pipeline e2e test to validate provisional->commit flow and invoiceable flagging
Chaos test: kill reset coordinator mid-phase and assert automated reconciliation recovers to consistent state
comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after spike with finance; prototype Anchor Resolver implemented in spike branch. Observed DST conversion oddity for Europe/Paris on March 28th. Next steps: formalize fallback when local timezone rule changes.

2026-03-02 - Carlos Mendes: Design review notes: prefer tenant-lease for leader election rather than new raft group. Concern about lock contention when many tenants reset simultaneously at 00:00 UTC—consider jittering or per-tenant reset windows with bounded spread.
2026-03-03 - Mei Lin (Finance): Confirmed billing must receive provisional adjustments as soon as prepare phase completes to avoid invoice mismatches when customer inspects usage mid-cycle.
2026-03-04 - Carlos Mendes: Implemented idempotency via correlation_id and provisional delta rows. Pushed branch eng/quota-anchors/implement. Started integration test for cross-region failover.

2026-03-05 - SRE (review): Added alert rule proposal for regional-drift > 0.1% and for leader-election failures exceeding 5% of tenants in a 24h window. Recommended adding metrics for reconciliation cost and number of corrective transactions per day.
